hints: If a maximum allowed segment sum T is fixed, greedily pack consecutive positive values until the next would exceed T.
This greedy process gives the fewest segments needed under T.
Binary-search the smallest T that needs at most k segments.
analogy: Test a proposed capacity by loading each segment as full as possible before starting the next.
example: For 2,4,7,3,5 with k=3, capacity 8 allows [2,4],[7],[3,5], whose largest sum is 8.
algorithm: Binary-search T between max(array) and total sum. Scan values, starting a new segment when current+x>T, and test whether segment count<=k.
correctness: For positive values, packing greedily delays each cut as long as possible and therefore minimizes the number of segments for capacity T; feasibility is monotone in T.
complexity: O(n log S) time and O(1) extra space, where S is the array sum.
